Do Blood Lipids Cause Coronary Heart Disease? A Two-Sample Mendelian Randomization

Pan-UK Biobank lipid GWAS (exposures) × FinnGen R12 coronary heart disease GWAS (outcome)

Author

Zi-Jie Liu

Summary

Genetic variants that raise a lipid trait act like a lifelong randomized “treatment”. Comparing their effects on the lipid with their effects on coronary heart disease (CHD) estimates the causal effect of the lipid itself.

  • LDL cholesterol and apolipoprotein B are causal for CHD. Per 1-SD higher LDL-C, CHD odds rise by 46% (IVW OR 1.46 (1.32 to 1.61)). All five robust methods agree.
  • Triglycerides look causal on their own, but not once ApoB is accounted for. In the multivariable model with ApoB and HDL-C, the TG odds ratio falls from 1.23 to 1.05 (1.00 to 1.11), consistent with TG-rich lipoproteins acting mostly through the number of ApoB-containing particles (the MR-Egger version leaves a small residual effect, OR 1.07).
  • HDL cholesterol keeps an inverse association (multivariable OR 0.89 (0.85 to 0.93)). HDL-raising drugs (CETP inhibitors, niacin) failed in trials, so this is more likely residual pleiotropy than a target (see Limitations).

Data and design

Exposure Outcome
Source Pan-UK Biobank, European ancestry FinnGen release 12, endpoint I9_CHD
Traits LDL-C, HDL-C, triglycerides, ApoB (inverse-rank-normalised, per SD) Coronary heart disease (log-odds)
Sample size ~400,000 per lipid ~500,000 (Finnish)
Build GRCh37 GRCh38, matched by rsID

The two samples do not overlap, which avoids the bias toward the observational association that sample overlap causes in two-sample MR.

Instruments. SNPs with p < 5×10⁻⁸ for the lipid, LD-clumped at r² < 0.001 within 10 Mb using 1000 Genomes European genotypes (prepared in project 02), mapped to rsIDs from the 1000 Genomes VCFs, then harmonised to the same effect allele. Palindromic SNPs were kept only when allele frequency resolved the strand.

Exposure Instruments Mean F-statistic
LDL-C 162 189
HDL-C 354 135
Triglycerides 292 142
ApoB 180 193

All F-statistics are far above 10, so weak-instrument bias is negligible.

How the methods guard against invalid instruments:

Method Assumption it relaxes
MR-Egger Pleiotropy allowed if independent of instrument strength (InSIDE); intercept tests directional pleiotropy
Weighted median Consistent if ≥50% of the weight comes from valid instruments
Weighted mode Consistent if the largest group of instruments with similar estimates is valid
Steiger filtering Drops SNPs that explain more variance in CHD than in the lipid (reverse direction)
Without LPA and 9p21 Removes two known non-lipid CHD loci: Lp(a) and CDKN2B-AS1

Each point is one SNP. The LPA variants (top of the LDL and ApoB panels) and the 9p21 variant (bottom) are the clearest outliers; removing them barely moves the estimates.

Cochran’s Q is large for every exposure (p < 1e-90), so there is substantial heterogeneity, and the MR-Egger intercept is non-zero for LDL-C (p = 0.002). That is why the random-effects IVW and the robust methods, not fixed-effect IVW, carry the conclusions.

Multivariable MR

Lipid traits share many variants, so univariable estimates can borrow each other’s effects. Multivariable MR estimates each trait’s direct effect.

Do the European instruments carry over to East Asians?

The same instruments’ lipid effects in the Pan-UKB East Asian sample (about 2,500 people) were regressed on their European effects.

Exposure SNPs Same direction EAS effect / EUR effect (slope)
ApoB 173 71% 0.51
HDL-C 338 67% 0.69
LDL-C 158 70% 0.59
Triglycerides 281 61% 0.44

Most instruments point the same way, but East Asian effects are about half the European size. Part of that is winner’s curse in the European discovery GWAS and noise in the small East Asian sample. An East Asian MR therefore needs East Asian instruments, for example from Biobank Japan or Taiwan Biobank.

Limitations

  • Pleiotropy is substantial (large Q). The robust methods agree, but none of them can rule it out completely, and the HDL-C result illustrates this.
  • Exposure effects are per SD of inverse-rank-normalised traits, not mg/dL.
  • FinnGen is a founder population; allele frequencies differ slightly from UK Biobank (harmonisation checks this).
  • Effect sizes are lifelong genetic differences and are larger than the effect of lowering lipids for a few years with a drug.

Reproduce

bash R/00_download_sumstats.sh    # stream and slim the public GWAS files
Rscript R/01_instruments.R        # select, clump and annotate instruments
Rscript R/02_outcome_harmonise.R  # look up in FinnGen and align alleles
Rscript R/03_mr.R                 # MR, MVMR, figures
quarto render report.qmd
